scores.evidence: Ephemeral microVM (Firecracker) with no credentials; egress only to a package mirror; destroyed after each run
scores.rationale: Mechanisms are accurate (App scoping, branch protection, microVM, hash-bound approval), with small inconsistencies like 'Tests run without network access' versus package-mirror egress and no mention of GitHub App token lifetime.

scores.evidence: It labels new issues, finds duplicates and asks for missing information. When a maintainer asks it to, it writes a fix in a sandbox and opens a draft PR.
scores.rationale: Covers triage and resolve with maintainer-gated fixes and explicit deferrals, though codebase retrieval for large repos and webhook/human-collision handling are thin.

scores.evidence: Trust boundary and write scope ... App can write issues, PRs and only `agent/*` branches; branch protection requires a human review; never merges
scores.rationale: Consistent design with clear phases and decision table; minor loose ends such as the sandbox network assumption and the 'merged PR' cost metric when ownership of merging is human.

scores.evidence: ≥150 red-team cases planted in issues, comments, repo files and test output; security reviewer review
scores.rationale: Validation is tied to specific risks, riskiest security checks come before exposure, thresholds are labeled assumptions, replay on hidden tests and canary and wave checks continue post-launch.

scores.evidence: Missing inputs (assumptions are stated; what changes if each is false is in brackets)
scores.rationale: Budgets labeled ASSUMPTION/UNKNOWN, each assumption has a change-if-false trigger, and the monthly cap is flagged as unknown and blocking.

scores.evidence: Caps cut off runaway jobs; jobs are idempotent
scores.rationale: Injection, exfiltration, sandbox escape, runaway loops and worker crash are covered concretely, but bot-to-bot loops, concurrent human edits and stale-issue collisions are not addressed.

scores.evidence: Rollback is a redeploy of the previous image plus an App kill-switch flag.
scores.rationale: Deploy, rollback, traces, alerts and kill switch are concrete per phase, but on-call ownership and incident response are not specified.

scores.evidence: Cost per merged PR | ≤$5 | ASSUMPTION (cheaper than an hour of engineer time)
scores.rationale: Per-job and daily caps, model routing and metering are covered with labeled assumptions, though the basis is thin and there is no build-cost or scaling model.

scores.evidence: R3: a single bad merge or leaked secret cannot be undone
scores.rationale: Decisions are classified by reversibility with revisit triggers, provider abstraction from Phase 0, and the one-way choices (trust boundary, sandbox, data privacy) are gated early.

scores.evidence: Operational complexity | 1 worker service + 1 sandbox runner
scores.rationale: Starts with a single LLM call slice, single-agent loop, and defers multi-agent, fine-tuning, memory, and auto-merge; the security machinery is justified by the stated worst failure.

scores.evidence: Phase 0: a real issue opened on an internal test repo gets one bot comment, "Suggested labels: …", from a single LLM call.
scores.rationale: Concrete first slice, dependency-ordered phases with exit checks, rollback per phase and failure fallbacks; a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: Triage acts on its own once V3 passes; resolve starts only on a maintainer's `/agent fix`; PRs stay drafts
App can write issues, PRs and only `agent/*` branches; ... minimum App permissions
Build a tool executor with an allow-list of tools and schema-validated arguments; the model cannot bypass it.
Ephemeral microVM (Firecracker) with no credentials; egress only to a package mirror; destroyed after each run
Replay 50 closed issues against their hidden tests
Shadow run on 300 labeled historical issues | Label accuracy ≥85%; duplicate precision ≥90%
PR review outcomes and label corrections are reviewed, then added to the eval set.
Caps per job (tokens, iterations, time) and per day (cost).
A hard 8k-token cap and a $1/day cap apply.
Every tool call and approval logged
Prompt plus retrieval (code search, issue embeddings)
idempotent per-issue jobs keyed by `(issue, event-id)`

traps.evidence: branch protection requires a human review; never merges
Untrusted text treated as data; allow-listed executor; no egress
A runaway loop is cut off at its cap and emits a metric.

note: Strong, risk-first, well-gated plan with clear assumptions and validation; weak on codebase retrieval detail, bot-loop/human-collision coordination, and incident ownership.
